properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] Install-Time npm/Bun Lifecycle Execution Beaconing Out Within Minutes
properties.description:
Detects the joint supply-chain pattern where a package-manager lifecycle hook (npm/pnpm/yarn/npx/node-gyp/Bun postinstall, preinstall, setup.cjs, setup_bun.js, bun_environment.js or binding.gyp install-time exec) spawns a script host that makes an outbound connection to a public host within minutes — the install-then-beacon chain, not any single rotating IOC. It matters this fortnight because the Mini Shai-Hulud / Miasma / Hades family and the Sapphire Sleet easy-day-js typosquat backdoored 140+ @mastra packages, 20 Leo Platform packages, 400+ AUR packages and propagated to Go and GitHub Actions ('Over 140 popular Mastra npm Packages Hit by Supply Chain Attack', 'From package to postinstall payload', 'Mastra npm Supply Chain Attack: 140+ Packages Backdoored via easy-day-js Typosquat', 'Mass npm Supply Chain Attack: 20 Leo Platform Packages Compromised', 'Miasma Malware Targets npm Packages and GitHub Actions', '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked'), all of which weaponise the install lifecycle to drop a second-stage stealer that immediately calls home. It spans install (lifecycle-hook code execution) into command-and-control (the post-install egress that pulls the second stage or exfiltrates secrets). It FIRES when a developer/CI host runs an install whose hook process is followed within five minutes by a public outbound connection; it does NOT fire on package installs with no install-time child egress, on purely registry-bound traffic, or on runtime application network calls long after install. Reference IOCs (`<c2_ip_list>`, `<c2_domain_list>`, `<sha256_list>`) are substitution slots only.

Rationale: Every article in this batch weaponises the same install-lifecycle primitive (postinstall/preinstall/binding.gyp/Bun bootstrap) to execute code that immediately reaches the network, so correlating the lifecycle-hook child process with public egress inside a tight window catches the shared TTP regardless of which package, scope, or rotating C2 IOC is in play.
properties.query:
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
let Window = 5m;
let InstallExec = DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","node-gyp.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe","npm","node","node-gyp","pnpm","yarn","npx","bun","sh","bash")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","bun.exe","node","bun","sh","bash","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("postinstall","preinstall","setup.cjs","setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","binding.gyp","node-gyp")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InstallProc = FileName, InstallCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
InstallExec
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"                       // skip lateral / registry-mirror RFC1918
    | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, NetProc = InitiatingProcessFileName
  ) on DeviceId
| where NetTime between (ProcTime .. ProcTime + Window)    // egress within 5m of the install hook
| project ProcTime, NetTime,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, ProcTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, InstallProc, InstallCmd,
          NetProc, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by ProcTime desc
